dest.intro: Choose a saved destination or create a new one.
dest.newHint: Local folder, SFTP server or Nextcloud
dest.etaLater: The estimated time appears once the files are counted.
dest.failingHint: Some checks failed. You can still continue, but the copy may fail.

dest.finishForm: Save or cancel the new destination first.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.tooBig: Not enough free space: {size} to send, {free} free at the destination.
analysis.scanErrors: {n} item could not be read | {n} items could not be read
analysis.reopened: Transfer reopened from the list: the counts are the saved ones.
analysis.noIssues: No name problems: everything is sent as it is.
analysis.intro: filebridge counts the files and checks whether any name would cause problems at the destination. Nothing has been copied yet.
analysis.countingHint: Large folders can take a few minutes. You can wait here or come back later.
analysis.errorHint: Check that the files and the destination are still reachable, then try again.
analysis.guidePendingTitle: {n} name needs your decision | {n} names need your decision
analysis.guidePending: Accept the suggested fixes in one click: they are the safe choice and only change the copy. Or review them one by one.
analysis.guideOk: All good: no name needs changing. Click “Next” to review and send.
analysis.guideFixed: All good: the names below are adjusted automatically in the copy so the destination accepts them. Your originals keep their names. Click “Next”.
analysis.tooBigHint: There isn't enough free space at the destination. Free some space there, or go back and choose fewer files.
analysis.symlinksHelp: Shortcuts (symbolic links) point to other files. They aren't copied, so the same thing isn't copied twice and nothing outside the chosen folders gets in.
analysis.scanErrorsHelp: Usually files you don't have permission to read, or that were removed while counting. They won't be copied.
analysis.preflightHelp: whether the destination is reachable, accepts writing, and how much space is free
analysis.namesHelp: Some systems refuse certain names (Windows, for example, refuses “:” and “?”). filebridge fixes the name only in the copy; the original file stays as it is.
analysis.waitHint: Wait for the analysis to finish.
analysis.guideLook: These names need you to read them before deciding. Open each group and choose.
analysis.notBulk: {n} name is left for you to read first: garbled names and names without a suggestion are never accepted in one click. | {n} names are left for you to read first: garbled names and names without a suggestion are never accepted in one click.
analysis.acceptSuggestions: Accept the suggestion | Accept the {n} suggestions
analysis.repairHint: Earlier transfers to {destination} may have left garbled names like these there. Repair names, in its ⋮ menu in Destinations, fixes them where they are.

nfc.title: {n} name with accents stored differently | {n} names with accents stored differently
nfc.explain: Fixed automatically. The text looks the same, but the accents are stored in a way other systems may not recognise (common in files from a Mac). They're converted to the standard form (NFC).
nfc.example: “café.txt” looks the same before and after; only the hidden bytes change

nextcloud-nfc.title: {n} name Nextcloud would not find | {n} names Nextcloud would not find
nextcloud-nfc.explain: Fixed automatically. Nextcloud only finds names whose accents are stored in the standard form (NFC), so they're converted.
nextcloud-nfc.example: “Relatório.pdf” looks the same, but Nextcloud would not list it without the fix

forbidden-chars.title: {n} name with characters the destination refuses | {n} names with characters the destination refuses
forbidden-chars.explain: Fixed automatically. The destination doesn't accept < > : " \ {'|'} ? * or control characters in names; each one becomes _.

trailing.title: {n} name ending in a space or dot | {n} names ending in a space or dot
trailing.explain: Fixed automatically. Windows doesn't allow names that end in a space or a dot, so they're removed.

reserved.title: {n} reserved Windows name | {n} reserved Windows names
reserved.explain: Fixed automatically. Windows keeps some names for itself (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1…); they get a _ in front.

nextcloud-reserved.title: {n} name Nextcloud reserves | {n} names Nextcloud reserves
nextcloud-reserved.explain: Fixed automatically. Nextcloud keeps some names for itself, like .htaccess; they get a _ in front.

collision.title: {n} name that would clash with another | {n} names that would clash with another
collision.explain: After the fixes, two different names would end up the same at the destination, and one would replace the other. “Accept” adds a number to this one; or edit it.
collision.example: “Photo.jpg” and “photo.jpg” on a disk that doesn't tell capitals apart → “photo (2).jpg”

encoding.title: {n} name written in an old encoding | {n} names written in an old encoding
encoding.explain: These names were saved by an older system (often Windows), not as UTF-8, so other systems can't read them. filebridge reads them as Windows-1252 and sends the readable name; the bytes are shown so you can check. A name it could only guess waits for you.

mojibake.title: {n} garbled name | {n} garbled names
mojibake.explain: These names look like they were once read with the wrong encoding and saved that way, which turns accents into pairs like “Ã³”. “Accept” uses the repaired name, on the right. Check first: a real name can look like this, so it is never fixed by itself.

length.title: {n} name too long for the destination | {n} names too long for the destination
length.explain: The destination doesn't take names (or paths) this long, so these files would fail. “Accept” shortens the middle of the name and keeps its start, end and extension; or edit it, or skip it.
length.example: “Relatório anual de atividades da associação 2023.pdf” → “Relatório anual…ação 2023.pdf”

issues.keptClash: Sent as “{name}”: the same name as another one, so sending waits until one of them changes.
issues.editTitle: Choose the name at the destination
issues.acceptTip: Use the fixed name shown on the right
issues.keepTip: Send with the original name, without this fix (refused if the destination can't take it)

issues.acceptAllTip: Use the suggested fix for all of them (recommended)
issues.keepAllTip: Send all of them with the original name
issues.bulkAdvice: Not sure? “Accept all” is the safe choice.
issues.encodingAdvice: The original bytes can't be kept: the destination only takes readable (UTF-8) names. Accept the reading, edit it, or skip.
issues.bytesTip: Technical view: the bytes of the name before (red) and after (green). They show the change when the text looks identical.
issues.editHint: Only the name changes, not the folder it's in.
issues.carriedTip: Copied from the transfer this one repeats. You can change it.
issues.selectMatching: Select the {n} pending one that matches | Select the {n} pending that match
issues.oneGroup: Selection cleared: one group at a time.

review.verifyHint: After copying, filebridge reads every file again at the source and at the destination and confirms they're identical (SHA-256). It takes longer, but you know for sure nothing was lost.
review.safety: Copy only: the source is never changed or deleted. Closing the window doesn't stop the transfer.

review.modeHelp: How the files reach the destination.

profile.name: Name

help.name: A name for you to recognise this destination in the list. Anything works.

help.knownHosts: The file listing the servers this computer already trusts. Leave empty to use the usual one.
help.target: The kind of system the destination uses; it decides which names need fixing. If unsure: a USB stick or disk also used on Windows → Windows; a NAS or Linux server → Linux.
help.case: When on, “Photo.jpg” and “photo.jpg” are two different files. Windows and macOS usually treat them as the same file.
help.password: Only if this server signs in with a password instead of a key. It is kept in your system's keyring (Keychain, Credential Manager, GNOME Keyring), never in filebridge's files.

hint.name: Just for you to recognise it.

hint.keyFile: Empty = the SSH agent of this computer (the usual case)

nextcloud.ncUserHint: The account that receives the files
nextcloud.folderHint: Empty = the top of that user's files
nextcloud.folderHostPath: This looks like a path on the server. Type a folder inside the Nextcloud user's files (e.g. Backup): filebridge finds the data folder by itself.
nextcloud.pickContainer: More than one container looks like Nextcloud. Which one?

runtime.proxmox-lxc: Nextcloud runs in a container on this Proxmox host.
runtime.host: Nextcloud runs on this machine itself (no Proxmox container).

nextcloud.advancedHint: only if the detection asks for it
nextcloud.detectTip: Connects and checks everything, step by step. Nothing is changed on the server.

help.ncUser: The Nextcloud account that receives the files: the login name, not the display name.
help.host: The address of the Proxmox node that runs the Nextcloud container, or of the machine Nextcloud runs on (its container, VM or server, e.g. its Tailscale address).
help.sshUser: The user filebridge logs in with over SSH on that server. It must be root or have passwordless sudo. Usually root.
help.folder: A folder inside that user's files. Empty puts the files at the top.
help.ctid: Proxmox only: the number of the container where Nextcloud runs. Leave empty and filebridge finds it.
help.installDir: Where Nextcloud is installed inside the container. Leave empty and filebridge finds it.

offline.title: Your transfers show here once the copy engine answers.
offline.body: Nothing is lost meanwhile: the transfers and destinations are kept by the engine, not by this window.

welcome.title: Copy without losing anything. And prove that everything arrived.
welcome.noDestination: You'll choose where the copy goes on the way: a disk, a server or Nextcloud.

source.title: Your originals are never touched
source.body: Nothing at the source is deleted, moved or renamed.

names.title: Names arrive right
names.body: Accents, forbidden characters and garbled names are fixed in the copy only.

proof.title: Proof that it all arrived
proof.body: Every file checked by SHA-256, with a report you can keep.

home.pausedByYou: Paused. It continues from the same point when you resume it.

tour.replay: Show the guide for this step

steps.title: Send in {n} steps
steps.body: Choose what to send, then where. filebridge checks every name, you review, and the copy starts. You can go back to an earlier step until you send.

add.title: Add what you want to send
add.body: Drag files and folders onto the window, or use the buttons. Add as many as you like: they all go to the same place, and nothing at the source changes.

recent.title: The same place again
recent.body: Folders you sent before are here: one click adds one. One on a disk that isn't plugged in shows as not found.

chosen.title: Check what you chose
chosen.body: Each item says what it is and how big. If one can't be sent (missing, a link, or already inside another folder) it says why, with a fix.

next.title: Then choose where it goes
next.body: Next is ready once there is nothing to fix. The files are counted after you choose the destination.

summary.title: What you're sending
summary.body: Every file was counted, and the destination checked: it can be reached, accepts writing and has room. Nothing has been copied yet.

decide.title: Decide in one click
decide.body: The suggested fixes are the safe choice: they change the name only in the copy. Accept them all here, or review them one by one.

names.title: Names the destination wouldn't take
names.body: Each group is one reason, with an example. Open a group to see every name and choose for each one: accept, keep, skip or edit.

next.title: Then review and send
next.body: Next is ready once every name is decided. You can still come back here before sending.

card.title: One card per destination
card.body: Where it is, how much space is left, and which names its file system refuses. Saved once, picked in every transfer.

actions.title: Test, browse, and the rest
actions.body: Test checks that filebridge can reach it and write; Browse shows its folders. The ⋮ menu edits it, repairs names already there, or deletes it (never its files).

new.title: Another place to copy to
new.body: An external disk, a server over SSH, or Nextcloud. Each one is checked before it is saved.

repair.title: Repair names at the destination
repair.lead: Names already in {folder} on {destination}, checked with the same rules as a transfer. Nothing is renamed until you confirm.
repair.label: Repair · {folder}
repair.buttonTip: Check the names already in a folder of this destination and fix them there
repair.readCount: {n} file so far | {n} files so far
repair.cleanBody: {n} file checked; nothing to rename. | {n} files checked; nothing to rename.
repair.howTo: These names would change. Decide the ones marked pending; “Skip” leaves a name (and, for a folder, what's inside) as it is.
repair.pending: Decide {n} name first | Decide {n} names first

confirm.title: Rename {n} name? | Rename {n} names?
confirm.onlyNames: Files are not copied, changed or deleted: only renamed. The old names stay in this repair's report.
confirm.taken: A new name that is already taken is left as it was and reported.
confirm.nextcloud: Nextcloud then rescans the folders that changed, so it shows the new names.

modeHint.webdav: Recommended: needs only Nextcloud's address and an app password, works from anywhere, and Nextcloud indexes the files as they arrive.
modeHint.direct: For big first migrations on your own network: writes straight into Nextcloud's data folder over SSH, then asks Nextcloud to index what arrived.

webdav.intro: filebridge signs in to Nextcloud with an app password, like the desktop and phone apps do. Nothing needs to be set up on the server.
webdav.https: Use https://: an app password must not travel unencrypted.

help.server: The address you open Nextcloud at in the browser, e.g. cloud.example.com. A WebDAV address copied from Nextcloud's Files settings works too, and is needed when you sign in with an email address or a company account.
help.appPassword: Create one in Nextcloud: Settings → Security → Devices & sessions → “Create new app password”. It can be revoked there at any time, and it is not your account password. filebridge keeps it in the system keyring.
help.folder: Where transfers go, inside the user's files, e.g. Backup/Fotos. It is created by the first transfer if it doesn't exist.

webdav.appPasswordHint: Not the password you sign in to Nextcloud with: with two-factor sign-in that one can't work here. Create one in Nextcloud under Settings → Security → Devices & sessions.

access.uses: Signs in with filebridge's own key

install.tip: Give this destination a key of its own, kept in the system keyring, so your personal SSH key is no longer used
install.title: Use filebridge's own key for “{name}”?
install.what1: filebridge makes a new key on this computer and keeps it in the system keyring, never in a file.
install.what2: It adds one line to the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of {who}, marked “restrict”: no interactive terminal, no tunnels, no forwarding. Nothing else on the server changes.
install.what3: From then on this destination signs in with that key instead of yours; your key stays where it is.
install.what4: It signs in with the new key before switching. If any step fails, everything is undone.
install.ok: Done: this destination now uses filebridge's own key.
install.unconfirmed: Installed, but not every check could be made: see the steps marked !.
install.failed: Not installed: each step below says what was undone.
install.failedUndo: Not installed, and the undo didn't finish: see the steps marked ✗ for what is left.

remove.tip: Delete filebridge's key from the server and the keyring, and check that it no longer signs in
remove.title: Remove filebridge's access to “{name}”?
remove.what1: filebridge deletes its own line from the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of {who}, and nothing else.
remove.what2: It tries the old key once more and checks that the server refuses it; if the server still accepts it, nothing else changes.
remove.what3: Only then does this destination sign in with your key file or SSH agent again, if it has one.
remove.what3Password: Only then does this destination sign in with its password again.
remove.what4: Last, it deletes the key from the system keyring.
remove.ok: Done: filebridge's key is gone and no longer signs in.
remove.unconfirmed: Removed, but not everything could be confirmed: see the steps marked !.
remove.failed: Not finished: see the step that failed.

access.offer: Finished sending to “{name}”? When you won't send there again, remove filebridge's key from the server.

hostKey.title: Trust this server?
hostKey.intro: filebridge has not connected to {host} before. Check that this is really your server before going on: someone on the network could be pretending to be it.
hostKey.howToCheck: Compare it with the fingerprint the server shows: ask whoever runs it, or run this on the server. Trust it only if they are the same.
hostKey.savedIn: It will be added to {file}, and this server will not be asked about again.
hostKey.changed: {host} presented a different key from the one saved in {file} (line {line}). filebridge will not connect.
hostKey.changedWhat: Either the server was reinstalled or its keys were replaced, or someone is intercepting the connection. If whoever runs the server confirms the change, remove the old line from that file and try again.
hostKey.unreachable: Could not check the server's key: {error}

result.verified: file copied and verified, one by one | files copied and verified, one by one
result.noDifferences: No differences: every file at the destination is identical to its original (SHA-256).
result.notVerified: Verification was off for this transfer: the copies weren't read back and compared.
result.problems: of {n} file copied | of {n} files copied
result.problemsSub: {problems} file needs a look: it failed, or differs at the destination. | {problems} files need a look: they failed, or differ at the destination.
result.failed: of {n} file copied before the transfer stopped | of {n} files copied before the transfer stopped
result.cancelled: of {n} file copied before it was cancelled | of {n} files copied before it was cancelled
result.cancelledSub: What arrived stays at the destination; nothing was deleted anywhere.
result.renamed: {n} name fixed for the destination | {n} names fixed for the destination
result.retries: retried by itself once | retried by itself {n} times
result.reclaim: You can free {size} at the source.
